Photograph: Manuel Balce Ceneta/AP US Senate Trump vows to push $1.8bn slush fund as Senate committee set to reconsider AG nomination After declaring ‘anti-weaponization’ fund ‘dead’, Trump reverses and says he’ll revive it despite Senate opposition Edward Helmore Sat 1 Aug 2026 10.31 EDT Last modified on Sat 1 Aug 2026 10.32 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The US Senate judiciary committee has scheduled a meeting early next week to consider Todd Blanche’s nomination for attorney general, as Donald Trump promised to revive the controversial $1.8bn “anti-weaponization” fund. The meeting, set for Tuesday, comes as Blanche’s confirmation ​has stalled over a dispute between the president and outgoing Republican senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis, who are seeking written confirmation that the justice department would not establish the proposed fund. A spokesperson for the committee said in a statement that Chuck Grassley, committee chair and Iowa Republican, “wants Todd Blanche’s nomination to be successful”. DoJ appears to ignore New Mexico deadline for key Epstein ranch files Read more “Grassley would like to see Blanche confirmed before the August recess as he has an excellent record restoring law and order and keeping Americans safe,” the statement added. Opponents of the president consider it a slush fund to compensate political allies for political lawfare; supporters say it is a vehicle to compensate individuals who claim they were wrongfully targeted by the government more broadly. “It is dead, but I wish ⁠it weren’t, to be honest with you. I think people were horribly treated, horribly abused,” Trump had said during a cabinet meeting on Friday. “I’d like to ⁠see them compensated for the pain.” At the cabinet meeting on Friday, Trump urged Republican senators to confirm Blanche and warned that they “will never get anybody like him” and repeated a claim that ​Cornyn was blocking Blanche because Trump had endorsed Cornyn’s Republican primary challenger Ken Paxton. “I’d be upset also,” ‌Trump said. “I fully understand it. He shouldn’t be that way. I shouldn’t be that way.“ Trump then slammed Cornyn and Tillis in a post on Truth Social on Saturday, claiming that both were upset because he had not endorsed them. Trump threatened to withdraw Blanche’s nomination, keep him on as acting attorney general and “push hard” for anti-weaponization bill. “Todd Blanche was a voice of reason!” Trump wrote. “It will immediately be back on the table, and I will get it done.” Blanche, Trump’s former personal attorney, has told senators that the fund was dead, but has so far not agreed to put that in writing. The “anti-weaponization” fund was crafted as part of a ⁠legal settlement between Trump and the justice department to resolve his $10bn lawsuit against the IRS over allegedly mishandling ​his tax records. Trump wrote that the fund “will not benefit me, but rather the great American Patriots who were hunted down like dogs and whose lives were unfairly and illegally destroyed”. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Around 2-3 times a day Sign up to Breaking News US Get the most important news as it breaks Preview latest after newsletter promotion Tillis has said those who attacked law enforcement during the 6 January 2021 riots should still be in prison and should not get a check from the federal government. Cornyn and Tillis also object to ​an IRS deal that would prevent tax audits of Trump and his associates. Tillis responded on Saturday, saying that despite Trump’s comments that the fund is dead, the president “clearly intends to resurrect the payout pot for punks either by inappropriately establishing another bogus fund or pushing Congress to vote for a bill that the majority of Republicans in the Senate would be against”. “It’s unfortunate that Todd Blanche, who I consider qualified for the job, will not be confirmed because of this reversal,” he said on X . “Hopefully, we can resolve this by Tuesday.” The back-and-forth over Blanche’s nomination, which is vigorously opposed by victims of Jeffrey Epstein over his handling of investigative files related to the late sex trafficker, now likely lies with backroom negotiations over the weekend. The same controversy dogged Trump’s original second-term attorney general, Pam Bondi, before she resigned. Cornyn and Tillis were reported to be close to backing Blanche as recently as Thursday. But with just more than two years left in Trump’s second term, Blanche may not need formal Senate confirmation to serve so long as his nomination is pending and not formally rejected or withdrawn. The seafarers were aboard the MV Gas Lisbon, the Liberia-flagged tanker transporting liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), when their ship was attacked. It burned down near the coastline of Romania on July 20. The two Filipino seafarers suffered burn injuries from the incident, while another Filipino crew member died on July 23. Tensions in Black Sea are brought on by the conflict between Russia and Ukraine. OWWA and the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) met with the seafarers upon their arrival at Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) Terminal 3, where they were also given airport assistance and special financial assistance. Representatives from their licensed manning agency were also present to provide post-arrival interventions, including temporary accommodations, medical assessment and other assistance before they are sent home to their families. DMW Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac earlier reported that 236 Filipino seafarers aboard 17 commercial vessels were affected by the attacks near Ukrainian ports. Three of them were killed, 15 were injured and one is still missing, while 217 are safe. A total of 89 Filipinos, including nine injured, have returned to the Philippines. Cacdac assured that repatriation efforts are ongoing. Romanian Foreign Ministry/Handout via REUTERS An F-18 fighter on a NATO air policing mission shot down a drone that illegally breached Romanian national airspace, the fourth unmanned aircraft shot down over the country this year, Romania's Defense Ministry said on Sunday. A spokesperson for NATO's military headquarters, U.S. Army Colonel Martin O'Donnell, said the alliance is constantly on watch and prepared to defend itself from any threat. "Additional details regarding Sunday’s incident remain under investigation, but the drone appears to be Russia n," he said. NATO member Romania shares a 614 kilometers (381 miles) land border with Ukraine and has reported repeated breaches of its airspace by Russia n drones over the past four years, as well as mines floating in the Black Sea across key trade and energy routes. news Trump Rejects New Russia Sanctions at NATO Summit Filled With Big Spending and Big Emotions Read more Romania's Defense Ministry did not specify the origin of the drone, saying it was detected by radar as it entered the country from neighboring Moldova, 24 kilometers north of the southeastern Romanian city of Galati. The F-18 jet, part of a Spanish NATO contingent deployed in Romania, "made radar contact with the target and received permission to engage," the ministry said in a statement, adding that the drone was shot down safely at 5:01 a.m. The ministry said that fragments from the destroyed drone appeared to have fallen in an uninhabited area between two villages. In July, Romanian F-16 fighter jet pilots shot down three Russia n drones breaching national airspace for the first time after dozens of such incursions since the start of Russia 's war in Ukraine. In May, a Russia n drone crashed into an apartment block in Galati during an overnight attack on neighboring Ukraine, injuring two people.
